tool.name: DiamondSure, DiamondView and photoluminescence
tool.measures: whether a diamond is natural or synthetic (HPHT, CVD), and whether it has been treated
tips: A “Refer” does not mean synthetic, only “to be examined”

steps.title: Three ways to make a diamond
steps.text: • Natural: formed in the Earth's mantle, billions of years ago. • HPHT (high pressure, high temperature): the conditions of nature are reproduced in a machine. • CVD: diamond is grown layer by layer, from a gas. All three are real diamonds: they pass the thermal tester. Yet their value is not the same, and you must be able to tell them apart.

steps.title: DiamondSure: the quick sort
steps.text: The DiamondSure analyses the UV transmission of the diamond, and sorts the stone into two groups: • Pass: consistent with an ordinary natural diamond; • Refer: “to be looked at more closely”. A “Refer” is not a condemnation: it only asks for a further examination.

steps.title: DiamondView: growth patterns
Photoluminescence
steps.text: Photoluminescence cools the stone with liquid nitrogen (77 K) and excites it with a laser. The lattice defects of the diamond (the H3, NV, silicon-vacancy and nickel centres) give off sharp lines. The combination of these lines is the signature of the growth mode, and it also betrays treatments, such as irradiation or HPHT annealing.

steps.title: The laboratory report
steps.text: At the end, a serious laboratory issues a certificate: the weight, colour, clarity, cut, and the statement natural or synthetic. A treated diamond (irradiated, HPHT, filled) or a fancy one loses its “colourless” diamond certificate. The statement changes the price completely: a natural diamond is worth far more than the same laboratory-grown diamond.

steps.title: To remember
steps.text: • Natural, HPHT and CVD diamonds look alike to the eye and to the thermal tester. • DiamondSure: quick sort; DiamondView: growth patterns; photoluminescence: signature of the lattice. • You always cross-check several results before concluding.
